A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLPF research, despite the changed title and emphasis. Their complete main texts and appendices support reliable comparison; equations, figures, tables, and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLPF experiments, repeated path measurements, PCA and SVD analyses, and post-training generalization results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original LLPF experiments and reports additional architecture evaluations, connections across training configurations, and interpolation-based continuity checks.

M1.justification: The two LLPF algorithms remain, but v4 adds a step_c contribution to MOVE and introduces the Follow Data Flow layer-ordering strategy, with distinct CCT7 and DLA schedules. Section 5 also specifies a connection procedure that targets a projection onto the destination variance sphere using adapted M2O, then concatenates an M2M path. These extend the procedure beyond v2's existing layer-wise framework.

E1.justification: v4 removes the ImageNet1k evaluation and its pretrained ResNet18 generalization study from v2 Section 5, eliminating the only large-scale image dataset evaluated by the work. MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 remain; all were already present in v2. Additional architectures change model configurations rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 expands the reported comparison beyond AutoNEB to include FGE and SPRO. FGE receives a cited worst-case loss of 0.022; SPRO receives qualitative comparison entries with loss unreported. These are literature-based comparisons across different architectures, and neither PDF establishes matched baseline reruns.

E3.justification: v4 adds evaluations using VGG11, DenseNet, EfficientNet-B0, RegNetX-200MF, and DLA configurations, plus connections between models trained with different weight decay. It adds training accuracy and continuity evaluation using 50 interpolation samples per segment in Figure 5. The shorter CCT7 FDF schedule is an additional experimental configuration; the earlier manual schedule and retained datasets' preprocessing remain documented.

E4.justification: v4 adds direct checks that interpolations between consecutive LLPF points maintain low loss, addressing continuity beyond the sampled points (Figure 5 and Appendix A.7). It also tests connections across weight-decay configurations. Conversely, v2's PCA layer diagnostics and SVD dimensionality analysis disappear. The 100-model variance/mean checks and below-0.006 path experiment are retained.

E5.justification: v2 specifies 200, 40, and 10 repetitions for its principal experiments; v4 uses the less specific 'at least 10' statement. Previously single-run supplementary comparisons in v2 Figure 8 receive variability bands in v4 Figure 9. Mean/standard-deviation reporting remains the convention. The PDFs do not establish that earlier run counts were reduced.

E6.justification: v4 reports additional successful architecture connections, connections across weight-decay settings, low-loss interpolants, and training-accuracy trajectories. It removes the PCA/SVD findings and the reported ImageNet accuracy improvement from 69.758% to 70.55%. The below-0.006 result already appears in v2 Figure 10; v4 Figure 6 retains its loss curve but removes distance and test-performance panels. AutoNEB's 0.016 minimum in v2 and 0.0324 worst-case loss in v4 are different statistics.

T1.justification: The low-loss and variance-sphere definitions, Equations 1–6, and norm–variance derivation are retained; the proof moves from Appendix A.3 to A.8. v4 introduces training-loss tolerance as the gap between terminal-mode loss and maximum path loss. This is a limited mathematical definition addition, without a new connectivity theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion claim a fully connected low-loss space, absence of parameter redundancy at the space level, diagnostic PCA visualizations, and improved generalization. v4 replaces these contributions with a focused empirical framework for connecting independently trained modes, emphasizing architectural breadth, reproducibility, and connections between models trained with different hyperparameters.

C2.justification: v4 removes interpretations linking PCA fluctuations to input features and residual connections, SVD spans to parameter nonredundancy, and generalization gains to incomplete hyperparameter search. It adds explanations of cross-sphere connections and explicitly qualifies cross-paper loss comparability. The lack of guaranteed test generalization was already acknowledged in v2; its dedicated limitations section is largely a relocation. Specific VGG16 and Adam-trained ResNet18 failure examples disappear.

D1.justification: v4 expands layer schedules and training configurations in Tables 2–4, adds implementation sources, and reports equivalent-epoch budgets alongside updated hardware and reference times in Table 6. It states that code and further settings are in supplementary material. However, v2's detailed recipe for the retained below-0.006 experiment is removed, along with several runtime entries and ImageNet-specific settings.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion shifts from singular learning theory and global loss-space geometry toward empirical mode connectivity. v4 adds substantial positioning around SPRO, layer-wise connectivity, spawning, and permutation methods, including Adilova, Benton, Ainsworth, Entezari, and Frankle. It explicitly distinguishes independent training from shared-pretraining and permutation settings, while removing much of v2's singular-learning and redundancy-related literature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Definitions become a standalone section preceding related work; the geometric/generalization section disappears; evaluation gains new subsections; and limitations receive a dedicated section. Terminology shifts toward modes and mode connectivity throughout.

P2.justification: v4 adds a comparison table and connection/continuity figures, expands appendix result grids and configuration tables, and adds training-accuracy axes to the main plots. LeNet panels move to the appendix, PCA figures disappear, and the stringent-loss experiment retains only its loss panel. The new layout also introduces Figure 1 caption overlap on page 6 and architecture mismatches between captions and panels in Figures 11–12.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially improves alignment between claims and evidence: v2 extrapolates finite path and SVD observations to global connectivity and nonredundancy, whereas v4 focuses on experimentally supported mode connections. Interpolation checks directly address the earlier gap between discrete outputs and claimed continuous paths, while broader architecture and unequal-weight-decay experiments support the revised scope. These gains outweigh reduced ImageNet coverage, loss of the detailed 0.006-loss recipe, and caption/layout defects. The cross-model comparison remains limited, but v4 now explicitly acknowledges that limitation.
